postings.title: Research Scientist (Remote/US/LATAM)
postings.descriptionText:
Research Scientist, LLM Evaluations & Benchmarking 

Anyone AI Labs
Reports to: CEO · Remote / LatAm / US

The role Evaluation is one of the hardest open problems in AI: we still don't have reliable ways to measure what frontier models can and can't do, and the field mostly runs on benchmarks that are saturated, contaminated, or measuring the wrong thing. You'll own that problem at Anyone AI, measuring frontier model capability. 

This is a research role at heart: you decide what a good evaluation  is  , design the benchmarks that prove it, and defend the methodology under lab scrutiny. You'll build frontier-grade evaluation packages across reasoning, coding, agents, tool use, and multi-modal — grounded in expert-verified truth, validated against multiple models, and QC'd to survive buyer-side review. 

Responsibilities 

● Evaluation research. Turn eval targets into original benchmark designs. Own the hard measurement questions: construct validity, item discrimination, headroom, reliability, contamination, and capability elicitation. Push toward evals that stay informative as models improve. 

● Benchmark development. Build evaluation packages with subject-matter experts, each with expert-verified ground truth, multi-model headroom results, and rigorous QC (calibration layers, severity-weighted rubrics, deterministic verifiers). 

● Experts. Recruit, calibrate, and review a pool across coding, agentic/tool-use, and STEM/reasoning. Be the final arbiter of correctness and frontier difficulty. 

● Lab relationships. Be a technical point of contact for labs, with CEO support. Understand what they're trying to measure and translate it into an evaluation design. 

● Delivery & dissemination. Turn lab requests into winning sample packages and own pilots end to end. Where the work generalizes, help turn it into public benchmarks and papers: we support publishing at venues like NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks, ICLR, and ACL.

What we're looking for 

● Research background in ML evaluation or benchmarking (a track record of published or open benchmarks, eval/measurement research, or equivalent hands-on work that labs have relied on). 

● Deep LLM/frontier-model benchmarking expertise, with real strength in code-model and agentic evaluation. 

● Fluency with the measurement problem itself: construct validity, psychometrics, rubrics, pass rates, headroom, contamination, and what makes a task genuinely discriminate a model. 

● Interest in the safety side of evaluation, capability elicitation, robustness, and measuring the things that are hardest to measure honestly. 

● Proven ability to hold a team or expert pool to a rigorous standard. 

● Comfort with the full research loop: framing the question, running the study, and writing it up. 

● Fluent English; Spanish a plus.

You will have the opportunity to challenge yourself while contributing to developing a revolutionary accelerated training program designed to invest in people from LatAm and help them master ML and AI.

Anyone AI is an equal opportunity employer. Location: Remote — LatAm / US



ROLE OVERVIEW

The Program Lead, AI Fellowship owns the curriculum and learning design for Anyone AI’s fellowship program.

You are responsible for keeping the program aligned with the latest developments in the AI industry and evolving market demand. You own the overall quality of the fellowship, including slides, exercises, projects, and learning materials.

You will also help build and maintain a strong instructor network by sourcing candidates, interviewing them, and ensuring their delivery meets the standards of the program.

A PhD or equivalent technical depth in AI is required, ideally combined with hands-on industry or applied research experience, so that the fellowship reflects how AI is actually practiced today.



RESPONSIBILITIES


CURRICULUM & LEARNING DESIGN

Own the fellowship syllabus, including learning objectives, curriculum sequencing, and how individual modules fit together to produce meaningful, practical skill development.


INDUSTRY-ALIGNED CONTENT

Oversee the team responsible for designing learning content, including slides, exercises, projects, and supporting materials. Ensure the curriculum stays current with AI industry practices, technological developments, and hiring demand.


PROGRAM QUALITY

Set and maintain the quality standard across all learning materials and program experiences. Review learner outcomes and delivery feedback and continuously improve the curriculum based on those signals.


INSTRUCTOR NETWORK

Help source instructors from Anyone AI’s network, interview and evaluate candidates, and brief and calibrate instructors so classroom delivery consistently meets the curriculum standard.


TECHNICAL & ACADEMIC LEADERSHIP

Act as the internal reference for what high-quality AI education should look like. Partner closely with program operations to ensure logistics and delivery decisions support—not dilute—the learning experience.



EXPERIENCE

 - Teaching experience in university courses, fellowships, bootcamps, corporate academies, or similar settings, including lecturing, facilitating, or leading technical cohorts.

 - Hands-on AI/ML experience in industry or applied research.

 - Experience interviewing or evaluating technical instructors, experts, or educators and maintaining a high standard for delivery.

 - Comfortable working in a dynamic environment with fast iteration and a high degree of ambiguity.
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - PhD in a technical field such as Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related STEM discipline, or equivalent deep technical expertise in AI.

postings.title: Application Security Engineer – CVE & Vulnerability Research
postings.descriptionText:
Anyone AI is recruiting experienced Application Security Engineers and Vulnerability Researchers for a specialized project focused on reviewing real-world software vulnerabilities, CVE reproductions, remediation approaches, and exploit verification environments.

We’re looking for security professionals with hands-on experience in penetration testing, vulnerability research, or application security who can determine whether vulnerabilities are reproduced accurately, fixes address the actual root cause, and security tests reliably demonstrate that an exploit has been mitigated.




WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON

You’ll review technical security tasks involving:

 - CVE vulnerability reproduction

 - Exploit proof-of-concepts

 - Vulnerability remediation and secure coding

 - Application security testing

 - Docker-based vulnerability labs

 - Exploit verification scripts

 - Security regression testing

 - CVSS, CWE, and vulnerability classification

 - Environment and configuration analysis

 - Edge cases and alternative attack paths

A key part of the role is determining whether a vulnerability environment accurately recreates the original attack conditions and whether a proposed fix genuinely eliminates the vulnerability without breaking legitimate functionality.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years of hands-on experience in application security, penetration testing, or vulnerability research

 - Strong understanding of CVE, CVSS, CWE, and common vulnerability classes

 - Experience identifying and remediating vulnerabilities such as:
   
   - SQL injection
   
   - Command injection
   
   - SSRF
   
   - Deserialization vulnerabilities
   
   - Buffer overflows
   
   - Privilege escalation
   
   - Access control issues
   
   - Security misconfigurations

 - Strong understanding of secure coding and vulnerability remediation

 - Experience reviewing or developing exploit proof-of-concepts

 - Experience validating whether security fixes address the root cause rather than only the immediate exploit

 - Proficiency with Docker and Docker Compose

 - Ability to provide clear, technically rigorous written feedback




WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Reviewing CVE reproduction environments for technical accuracy

 - Determining whether vulnerabilities faithfully reproduce the original attack vector and impact

 - Evaluating proposed security fixes and remediation strategies

 - Reviewing test suites that verify both:
   
   - Normal application functionality remains intact
   
   - The original exploit no longer succeeds

 - Identifying incomplete fixes and alternative exploitation paths

 - Reviewing Docker environments for correct software versions, services, networking, and configuration

 - Detecting potential regressions or new vulnerabilities introduced by a fix

 - Providing recommendations for improving vulnerability reproductions, fixes, and verification logic




NICE TO HAVE

 - OSCP, GPEN, GWAPT, or equivalent security certification

 - Experience with responsible vulnerability disclosure or CVE reporting

 - Experience maintaining exploit proof-of-concept code

 - Experience writing automated security tests using tools such as:
   
   - Python
   
   - requests
   
   - curl
   
   - pwntools
   
   - Custom exploit harnesses

 - DevSecOps experience

 - Familiarity with SAST, DAST, and CI/CD security tooling

 - Experience developing or reviewing cybersecurity assessments or technical security challenges

 - Experience with AI evaluation, RLHF, or technical data projects




ENGAGEMENT

Work Type: Remote
Engagement: Part-time, project-based consulting
Focus: Application security, vulnerability research, CVE reproduction, and remediation

This role is ideal for security engineers who enjoy understanding how vulnerabilities actually work, reproducing exploits in controlled environments, evaluating security fixes, and identifying subtle gaps that traditional testing may miss.

FINANCIAL ANALYSIS & ACCOUNTING EXPERT

Help shape the future of AI by designing realistic financial analysis and accounting tasks that challenge advanced AI agents.

 - Location: Remote

 - Type: Contract / Part-time

 - Commitment: 20 hours/week

 - Compensation: US$30–60/hour

 - Project duration: 2 months, with potential extension

 - Availability: Immediate start


ABOUT THE ROLE

At Anyone AI, we create high-quality training and evaluation data for frontier AI models. We're looking for Financial Analysts and Accounting Experts with practical experience in financial modeling, accounting, budgeting, forecasting, reconciliation, and financial reporting.

You'll develop and validate realistic financial tasks that assess whether AI agents can analyze financial information, build accurate models, identify discrepancies, interpret financial statements, and complete complex professional workflows. Your expertise will help establish reliable reference solutions and meaningful evaluation criteria.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design realistic financial analysis and accounting tasks based on corporate finance and business operations.

 - Build and validate financial models, forecasts, operating budgets, and cash flow projections.

 - Analyze balance sheets, income statements, cash flow statements, and supporting financial documentation.

 - Prepare financial reconciliations, journal entry analyses, and variance reports.

 - Develop tasks involving financial planning, investment analysis, valuation, and business performance assessment.

 - Identify inconsistencies, missing transactions, incorrect formulas, and reconciliation errors.

 - Create reference solutions with transparent calculations, documented assumptions, and verifiable financial outputs.

 - Review AI-generated financial analyses for accuracy, completeness, and logical consistency.

 - Collaborate with technical contributors to establish reproducible tasks and objective evaluation criteria.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strong understanding of financial statements, accounting principles, and financial modeling.

 - Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets, including financial formulas, data analysis, and model validation.

 - Experience preparing financial forecasts, budgets, reconciliations, or management reports.

 - Ability to interpret complex financial documentation and identify inconsistencies.

 - Strong analytical thinking and attention to numerical accuracy.

 - Ability to explain financial assumptions, calculations, and conclusions clearly.

 - Strong written English communication skills.

 - Experience with ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, or NetSuite.

At Anyone AI, we create high-quality training and evaluation data for frontier AI models.

We’re looking for experts to evaluate personalized AI conversations using information available through connected digital services and prior activity.

In this role, you’ll have natural, back-and-forth conversations with two versions of an AI assistant and compare your experiences. Your feedback will help assess how effectively each assistant uses relevant information, understands your context, and responds to your needs.

postings.title: Head of Payments
postings.descriptionText:
ABOUT THE ROLE

As our Head of Payments, you will own payment performance end-to-end, with a strong focus on authorization rates, recurring payments, transaction routing, chargebacks, compliance, and payment costs.

This is a highly hands-on role with a significant focus on the US payments ecosystem. You’ll work directly with payment data, PSPs, acquirers, and internal teams to identify opportunities, solve performance issues, and drive measurable improvements across the payment lifecycle.

At Acentecom, we believe that a strong payments ecosystem is essential to creating seamless customer experiences and enabling sustainable growth. We’re looking for someone who understands the details behind payment performance and can turn that expertise into measurable business impact.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN

 - Own and continuously improve front-end authorization rates, identifying decline patterns and opportunities to increase successful initial transactions.

 - Own and continuously improve recurring and subscription authorization rates, optimizing retries, dunning, timing, and recovery strategies to maximize successful rebills.

 - Own transaction routing and cascading, continuously optimizing how transactions are routed across the payments ecosystem to improve approval performance and resilience.

 - Own chargeback performance and card-network monitoring, including VAMP and other Visa and Mastercard requirements, ensuring risk metrics remain within healthy thresholds.

 - Drive payment cost optimization, understanding the economics behind processing and working directly with PSPs and acquirers to optimize pricing, fees, and commercial terms.

 - Use payment data to diagnose issues and identify opportunities, translating decline codes, authorization trends, dispute data, and provider performance into concrete actions.

 - Partner directly with PSPs, acquirers, card networks, and internal teams to resolve payment issues and continuously improve performance.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - Strong hands-on payments experience within high-volume e-commerce, subscription, DTC, or a similarly complex consumer business.

 - Deep experience with the US payments ecosystem, including payment processing, acquiring, authorization behavior, card networks, and recurring payments.

 - Proven ownership of initial and recurring authorization rates, with experience identifying and implementing changes that materially improve payment performance.

 - Strong hands-on experience with MIDs, PSPs, acquirers, transaction routing, cascading, retries, and dunning optimization.

 - Deep understanding of chargebacks, disputes, fraud, and card-network monitoring programs, including VAMP and Visa/Mastercard thresholds.

 - Strong commercial understanding of payments, including processing costs, pricing models, provider fees, and PSP/acquirer negotiations.

 - Strong analytical skills and the ability to work directly with payment data, dashboards, decline codes, approval trends, and dispute metrics to identify problems and drive solutions.

 - A highly proactive, ownership-driven approach. You’re comfortable getting into the details, solving problems directly, and taking accountability for payment performance rather than operating only at a strategic level.

 - Strong communication and cross-functional skills, with the ability to work effectively with Engineering, Finance, Customer Support, and external payment partners.

postings.title: Treasury Analyst
postings.descriptionText:
As our Treasury Analyst, you will own the day-to-day visibility and accuracy of our cash position across a multi-brand, multi-entity DTC e-commerce business. You’ll make sure we know where our cash is, how it’s moving, and what we expect it to look like ahead, giving the team reliable data to make better financial decisions.

This is a highly hands-on role for someone who is comfortable working across banks, payment processors, legal entities, and currencies. You’ll manage cash reporting and forecasting, processor and bank reconciliations, intercompany activity, payment runs, and working capital while helping us build more scalable and reliable treasury processes.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN

 - Maintain an accurate daily consolidated cash position across all legal entities and banking partners.

 - Build and maintain a rolling 13-week cash forecast, identifying and explaining key changes, risks, and variances week over week.

 - Reconcile payment processor settlements to bank deposits and the general ledger, including settlement timing, reserves, and deposit mechanics.

 - Track and document intercompany transfers across entities, keeping balances, schedules, and supporting documentation accurate and current.

 - Prepare payment runs by gathering approved invoices, scheduling payments, and maintaining clear supporting documentation for approval.

 - Maintain working capital reporting across supplier payment terms, deposits, balance schedules, and cash conversion cycles, updating cash models as terms change.

 - Monitor chargebacks and disputes and maintain clear visibility into their impact on cash.

 - Track merchant account health, including reserve levels, processing limits, and decline patterns, identifying and escalating anomalies early.

 - Maintain accurate bank account records across entities, including signatories, access, and mandates.

 - Support month-end close through accurate and timely cash and bank reconciliations.

 - Help standardize cash forecasting, settlement reconciliation, and treasury processes as we continue building a more scalable financial infrastructure.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 3+ years of hands-on experience in treasury, cash management, financial operations, payments reconciliation, or a related role.

 - Strong experience reconciling high-volume transaction data across payment processors, marketplaces, banks, or similar environments.

 - Experience building and maintaining cash forecasts, ideally including rolling short-term cash forecasting.

 - Strong understanding of payment processor settlements, including timing differences, reserves, deposits, and reconciliation.

 - Experience working across multiple legal entities and currencies.

 - Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills, with the ability to build and maintain reliable financial models rather than simply work from existing templates.

 - Experience with accounting platforms such as QuickBooks Online and payment processors such as Adyen, Stripe, or similar tools.

 - Familiarity with subscription and rebill businesses and the impact of chargebacks, disputes, reserves, and processing performance on cash.

 - Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the persistence to investigate discrepancies across multiple systems until they reconcile.

 - A highly proactive and autonomous approach. You’re comfortable identifying issues early, investigating root causes, and driving them through resolution without requiring detailed direction.

 - Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to maintain accurate documentation and clearly explain cash movements, variances, and risks.

 - Fluent English.

postings.title: Software Engineer, Platform Experience
postings.descriptionText:
MEET SIENA

Siena is the Agent of Record for CX, built for consumer brands like Spanx, FIGS, Brooklinen, and Grüns.

It runs as a connected multi-agent stack on top of a shared intelligence layer: agents that sell, support, listen, handle social and voice across the entire customer journey, turning every conversation into signal you can act on.



THE TEAM

We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do.

We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock.

If you want to set the bar rather than follow one, keep reading.


THE ROLE

You take the hardest problems customers hit in production and solve them end to end: a webhook that stopped firing, an agent filling the wrong parameter, a report that won't reconcile. You find the real cause, work the customer to resolution, then build the automation so it doesn't come back. This is the front door to deployment and platform work at Siena, with a clear path into Forward Deployed Engineering or deeper platform work.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own hard problems end to end: trace, reproduce, fix, or hand engineering a clean reproduction. Get on the call when that's the fastest path

 - Debug the agents and the prompts. Diagnose whether a misfire is prompt, knowledge base, config, or model, then fix it so it holds under real traffic

 - Build so it doesn't happen twice. For every fix, ship the runbook or tool that stops it recurring

 - Close the loop to Product. Surface patterns, not one-offs, backed by metrics

 - Raise the team's floor. Lift what the whole team can resolve, not just what you can

 - Know where your scope ends. Escalate genuine product bugs and outages with a clean reproduction, not a shrug

 - Within 90 days, name the top recurring failure patterns and attack them at the root, not just patch symptoms


WHO YOU ARE

The Bar: If you're missing any of these, this isn't the role for you.

 - You solve problems end to end. Given a customer, some logs, and a vague symptom, you find the break and can tell a customer-side cause from a product bug

 - You're fluent with AI agents and prompts. You've built or debugged LLM workflows and know how they break: prompts, knowledge bases, retrieval, the gap between test and live

 - You're excited to build automation, not just fix what's in front of you. You think in leverage. This is the signal that matters most

Strong Signal: Not dealbreakers, but what separates a good hire from a great one.

 - You like talking to customers. You'll get on a call and resolve the real problem live, not just the reported one

 - Comfortable in our core stack (Node.js, TypeScript, React, Express) or close enough to ramp fast

 - Fluent with AI coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent) to script, clean data, or navigate a new codebase fast

 - You own problems nobody assigned you, and you make the people around you better through docs and walkthroughs

Nice to Have: Bonus, not required.

 - Observability tooling (Grafana, Honeycomb, Sentry)

 - Internal tooling that turned manual work into a system

 - Ecommerce or DTC exposure

Not a Fit If:

 - You stop at "it's not our bug" instead of finding the real cause

 - You'd rather build the fix than talk to the customer who hit it

 - You want a backlog of well-scoped tickets, not ambiguous production fires


WHY SIENA?

Real ownership. You will own problems, not tasks, with the autonomy to solve them your way and the trust to do it without a manager in your inbox.

Work that ships and matters. What you build reaches real consumer brands fast.

A category we are creating. The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in.

A team that respects your judgment. Globally distributed, async-first, low bureaucracy. We hire adults and treat you like one.

Great salary plus equity or stock grants. Own a piece of what you build.

Learning budget. If you are growing, so are we.

AI-fluency by default. Few places will push your work with production AI further or faster.


OUR VALUES

The people who thrive here are curious, customer-obsessed, and take ownership without being asked. They fix problems first and explain later. They're direct about feedback - both giving and receiving it - because they care more about getting things right than being polite.

They maintain high standards while moving at startup speed, and they build real relationships with teammates because they know that's how great work gets done. When things get tough, they adapt and keep pushing forward.


OUR APPROACH TO AI

The people who thrive here treat AI like a natural extension of themselves. They've built their own ecosystem of agents - some for research, others for debugging, writing, analysis, or writing code. They know which AI works best for what problem.

Everyone gets premium accounts (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity Pro, Cursor, Lovable) plus a quarterly budget for new tools. But the magic happens in how we share knowledge. Demo days where someone shows off a clever workflows. Slack threads about which model handles a specific use case better. Learning from each other's AI workflows.

At Siena, we're not just looking for people who can do a job. We're looking for people who want to break boundaries, create the future, and reshape industries. If that's you, we look forward to your application.


HOW WE HIRE

We use AI-assisted screening tools as part of our hiring process. All decisions are made by humans. You can request a human-only review at talent@siena.cx.

Siena provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gende

postings.title: Especialista de Producto - Argentina
postings.descriptionText:
Sobre Halter:

En Halter, nuestra misión es ayudar a los productores y ganaderos a gestionar sus operaciones de forma más productiva y sustentable. Nuestros clientes usan Halter para liberarse de las limitaciones de las prácticas convencionales. ¿Te imaginás ver a 500 animales levantarse y caminar tranquilamente hacia su próxima parcela? Sin cuatriciclos, sin perros, sin alambrados. Solo un rodeo caminando a su ritmo. La gente dice que parece magia. Nuestros clientes están revolucionando el pastoreo con Halter. Está cambiando vidas y transformando toda una industria. 

La gente se suma a Halter para hacer un trabajo con propósito. Al unirte a nosotros, vas a estar resolviendo problemas desafiantes dentro de un equipo de primer nivel y una cultura pensada para el alto rendimiento. Nuestro equipo piensa distinto, trabaja más duro y se compromete más. Estamos comprometidos a generar un cambio real en el mundo — no es fácil, y la verdad es que nos encanta que sea así de difícil. 

Contamos con el respaldo de inversores de primer nivel como Founders Fund, Bessemer Venture Partners, BOND, DCVC, Blackbird, Promus Ventures, Peter Beck de Rocket Lab e Icehouse Ventures. 

Para saber más, visitá nuestro LinkedIn e Instagram. 

Estamos buscando un Especialista de Producto que actúe como el principal representante de Halter en América del Sur durante nuestro lanzamiento en la región. Este es un rol pionero. Vas a trabajar directamente con nuestros primeros productores mientras desplegamos Halter en sus campos, aprendiendo qué hace falta para que el producto funcione de manera brillante en este entorno, y transmitiendo esos aprendizajes al resto de la empresa para que podamos construir e iterar en consecuencia. 

Vas a trabajar de cerca con la casa central de Halter en Nueva Zelanda y con nuestros equipos comerciales en América del Sur para asegurarte de que el producto entregue valor innegable desde el primer día y que estemos construyendo lo correcto para nuestros productores. 

Halter es una de las AgTech de más rápido crecimiento del mundo, y la tecnología más transformadora disponible para el pastoreo a base de pasturas. Con los collares y la app de Halter, los productores pueden cercar y mover virtualmente su ganado, y monitorear en tiempo real la ubicación y el comportamiento del mismo. 

Buscamos personas con visión amplia que entiendan cómo hacer que las cosas sucedan — gente que resuelve problemas de forma natural y se siente cómoda en un entorno dinámico y de alta energía donde va a ser desafiada a diario. Nuestra persona ideal es alguien profundamente comprometido con entender nuestro producto y las necesidades de nuestros clientes. Sobre todo, te va a importar el ganado y los productores que trabajan con él, y vas a defender sus intereses en toda la

organización. 

Se requiere disponibilidad para viajar a nivel nacional e internacional en este rol. 

 

Sobre el rol:

¿Cómo podría ser tu día a día? 

• Salir a los campos para ayudar a desplegar Halter con nuestros primeros clientes — esto es trabajo de campo, no de escritorio. 

• Construir relaciones sólidas con nuestros productores pioneros, entender en profundidad cómo operan y aprender qué necesita hacer el producto para entregar valor real en este contexto. 

• Transmitir esos aprendizajes de forma clara y rigurosa a nuestros equipos de producto e ingeniería en Nueva Zelanda, para que siempre estemos construyendo lo que más importa. 

• Ayudarnos a entender los matices de la producción ganadera en América del Sur — los animales, la tierra, las prácticas — y compartir ese contexto en toda la empresa. 

• Pensar de forma crítica sobre el producto de principio a fin e identificar qué necesitamos corregir, mejorar o construir a continuación. 

• Trabajar con nuestros primeros clientes para asegurarte de que estén aprovechando al máximo Halter y viendo resultados reales. 

• Colaborar con el equipo comercial para mantener una fuerte alineación a medida que escalamos. 

• Hacer todo lo necesario para que Halter triunfe en Sudamérica. 


Lo que buscamos: 

• Experiencia trabajando en la producción ganadera de América del Sur. Esto es requisito excluyente. 

• Pasión por los animales y el futuro de la ganadería en la región. 

• Interés por la tecnología y genuina curiosidad por cómo funciona nuestro producto. 

• Un comunicador sólido que pueda traducir lo que ve en el campo en feedback claro y accionable para un equipo remoto de producto e ingeniería. 

• Capacidad demostrada para pensar de forma crítica ante un problema y llegar a conclusiones sólidas e innovadoras. 

• Comodidad con la incertidumbre. Esta es una entrada temprana al mercado y las cosas van a ser imperfectas; vas a prosperar con eso en lugar de frustrarte. 

• Aprendizaje rápido con las ganas de trabajar duro junto a un equipo que está haciendo cosas que nunca se hicieron antes. 

• Una actitud de "manos a la obra" con la resiliencia para superar los desafíos. 

• Disponibilidad para viajar y trabajar de forma flexible, incluyendo fines de semana cuando sea necesario.

• Se requiere dominio del idioma inglés para colaborar con la casa central.

El dominio del inglés es un requisito para esta posición. El proceso de selección incluirá entrevistas en inglés y una parte significativa del trabajo diario también se desarrollará en este idioma. Buscamos personas que se sientan cómodas comunicándose, participando en conversaciones profesionales y trabajando efectivamente en inglés. Si no te sentís cómodo/a manteniendo conversaciones profesionales en inglés, esta posición probablemente no sea adecuada para vos.



Sumate al equipo:

Halter está comprometida con promover un lugar de trabajo diverso e inclusivo — un espacio donde cada uno pueda ser uno mismo y hacer el mejor trabajo de su vida. Collars, towers, and accessories need to be packed, freight coordinated, and delivered on a rapid timeline. When a deployment runs well, it feels seamless. When it doesn’t, everyone feels it. We are looking for someone to come in and run our dispatch process like a clinic.

You will own the end-to-end flow of hardware going out to new customers. Think of yourself as the air traffic controller of our dispatch operation - directing traffic, clearing bottlenecks, spotting risks early, and keeping everything moving at pace.  - Keep our internal teams in South America and Auckland HQ aligned and informed

 - Dive into the details when something doesn’t look right

 - Like running a tight ship and take pride in operational excellence

 - Can zoom into the detail without losing sight of the bigger picture

 - Are confident holding partners accountable

 - Stay calm under pressure and enjoy high-tempo environments

 - See problems as puzzles, not blockers

 - Are comfortable with ambiguity - this is an early-stage market entry and things will be imperfect

Candidates should feel comfortable communicating, participating in professional conversations, and working effectively in English. If you are not comfortable having professional conversations in English, this role may not be the right fit for you.


BONUS POINTS FOR:

 - Experience in a startup, scale-up or agricultural technology business.

 - Knowledge of cattle production or rural South America.

At Halter, we’re building world-class virtual fencing technology that transforms the way farmers and ranchers work. We tackle complex, real-world problems with technical solutions, helping farmers lift productivity, care for their animals, and farm more sustainably.

We’re looking for a Virtual Fencing Support Specialist to join our Guidance Operations team. This is a great role for someone who’s passionate about ag, understands farming deeply and thrives on problem solving.

This role sits right at the intersection of tech and farming. We’ll train you to become an expert in virtual fencing; understanding the technology inside out, and how animals interact with it. You’ll work in a small, focused team handling the trickier support queries we get from farmers, digging into data, diagnosing issues, and helping deliver world-class support.


About the role
With about a million collars online, there’s always something interesting to dig into. Farmers reach out via our in-app chat, and your job is to get to the bottom of their questions and issues. You’ll use data from the collars to replay events and figure out exactly what happened.
When a new farm starts with Halter, their cows go through a training process. In this role, you’ll be monitoring how that’s going, using data to track progress and reaching out to farmers to offer support, insights, or advice as needed.
Every time we release a new version of firmware, it has to be thoroughly tested before it hits the field. You’ll start by walking the collar around like a cow (seriously), then dive into the data to make sure everything’s working as expected as we roll it out to the wider fleet.

You’ll spend most of your days on the R&D farm near Morrinsville. We turned the old calfbarn into an office with prime views of our farm. Once or twice a fortnight, you’ll head up to our HQ in Auckland to work closely with our support and onboarding teams, making sure our farmers get the best support possible. While we aim to solve most issues remotely, sometimes you’ll be out on customers’ farms, hands-on, helping them directly.

 - You’re passionate about agriculture and want your work to make a difference.

By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard. 

We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund https://foundersfund.com, Bessemer Venture Partners https://www.bvp.com/, BOND, https://www.bondcap.com/ DCVC https://www.dcvc.com/, Blackbird https://www.blackbird.vc/, Promus Ventures https://www.promusventures.com/, Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures https://www.icehouseventures.co.nz/?utm_term=icehouse%20ventures&utm_campaign=Brand+Keywords&utm_source=adwords&utm_medium=ppc&hsa_acc=4064636360&hsa_cam=16902737884&hsa_grp=134004309485&hsa_ad=592971340272&hsa_src=g&hsa_tgt=kwd-1082530126230&hsa_kw=icehouse%20ventures&hsa_mt=b&hsa_net=adwords&hsa_ver=3&gclid=Cj0KCQjw2v-gBhC1ARIsAOQdKY0J0DepRVFDmjQlAkJPbZuQnLSA5UVzUzOXYiPxkjX-SeVa513_BhkaAr-MEALw_wcB.

About our Talent Pool.

Are you eager to explore opportunities at Halter, but can't find the right one advertised today? You're in the right place. We understand that there may not currently be a role for you here, but we’re still keen on hearing what you could bring to Halter! 

Feel free to submit your CV or LinkedIn profile to us and we’ll keep your profile on hold in case there might be a role in the future for you! 

This is an ‘expression of interest’ talent pool so we may not get back to you right away but you’ll definitely be on our radar! And don’t feel you need to stop there! Please feel free to follow us on LinkedIn and keep an eye on our careers site. 

We are growing rapidly so if you see a role advertised that sounds like you let us know by hitting apply. We’ll definitely be in touch with you. 

We're hiring all over New Zealand, Australia and the USA.





What we’re looking for.

 - Software, Digital Product, Firmware, Data, Systems, & Machine Learning

 - Hardware, Production, Tradesman & Supply Chain

 - Sales & Business Development

 - Customer Success, Account Management, & Field Support

 - Research & Development

 - Marketing & Creative

 - Strategy & Operations

 - People & Talent




JOIN OUR TEAM

Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement. If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch!

Please also feel free to check out the careers page https://www.halterhq.com/careers for more information on working at Halter and don't forget to follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.




WHY OUR TEAM LOVES WORKING AT HALTER:

 - Work that genuinely matters. Every now and again a company comes along that transforms an entire industry and leaves the world in a better place. Our team gets to be part of something truly meaningful, helping farmers improve their livelihoods, spend more time with their families, and build more sustainable operations.

 - Spectacular people solving hard problems. Our culture is designed for talented people to do work that changes lives. The team is filled with diverse, kind, and driven people who push each other to do their best work. You'll be thrown into the deep end, tackling complex challenges and building something tangible that solves real problems.

 - You'll grow here. Autonomy, mastery, and learning define how we work. You'll have the freedom to work on interesting problems, master new skills, and continuously develop yourself, both through your role and our $1,000 personal growth fund.

 - This isn't easy, and we love that it's hard. Working at Halter will be the most rewarding and the most challenging work of your life. We move fast, take bold bets, and work hard to reshape an entire industry. As one team member put it: "Joining Halter is a bit like strapping yourself to a rocket ship, but it's an epic journey to be a part of!"

About the role:

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the Northern region of Arkansas. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the customer to different teams across Halt

We're looking for a Product Specialist to be Halter's boots on the ground as we launch Halter in South America. This is a pioneer role. You'll be working directly with our earliest producers as we deploy Halter onto their farms, learning what it takes to make the product work brilliantly in this environment, and feeding those insights back to the rest of the company so we can build and iterate accordingly.

You'll work closely with Halter's HQ in New Zealand and our commercial teams in South America to make sure the product delivers undeniable value from day one  and that we're building the right things for South American producers.

Halter is one of the world's fastest-growing agritech companies, and the most transformative technology available in pasture-based grazing. With Halter's cattle collars and app, producers can virtually fence and shift their cattle, and proactively monitor cattle locations and behaviour.

We're looking for big thinkers who know how to get stuff done — people who are natural problem-solvers and are comfortable in a dynamic, high-energy environment where they'll be challenged daily. Our ideal person is someone deeply committed to understanding our product and our customers' needs. Above all, you'll care about the cattle and the producers who work with them, and you'll champion their interests across Halter.

National and International travel will be required in this role. 



About the role


What your day could look like:

 - Getting out onto farms to help deploy Halter with our first customers — this is hands-on work, not desk work.

 - Building close relationships with our pioneering producers, deeply understanding how they operate, and learning what the product needs to do to deliver real value in this context.

 - Feeding those learnings back clearly and rigorously to our product and engineering teams in New Zealand, so we're always building what matters most.

 - Helping us understand the nuances of South American cattle production. The animals, the land, the practices and sharing that context throughout the company.

 - Thinking critically about the product end-to-end and identifying what we need to fix, improve, or build next.

 - Working with our first customers to make sure they're getting the most out of Halter and seeing real results.

 - Partnering across the commercial team to maintain strong alignment as we scale.

 - Whatever else it takes to make Halter succeed in South America.


What we're looking for:

 - Experience working in South American cattle production. This is a must-have.

 - Passionate about animals and the future of agriculture in the region.

 - Tech-savvy and genuinely curious about how our product works under the hood.

 - A strong communicator who can translate what they're seeing in the field into clear, actionable feedback for a remote product and engineering team.

 - Proven ability to think critically about a problem and reach strong, innovative conclusions

 - Comfortable with ambiguity. This is an early-stage market entry and things will be imperfect; you'll thrive on that rather than be frustrated by it.

 - Fast learner with the drive to work hard alongside a team doing things that have never been done before.

 - A get-stuff-done attitude with the resilience to push through challenges.

 - Willing to travel and work flexibly, including weekends when needed.

 - Spanish fluency required.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.

 

This role covers the Central region of Kansas. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.

 


WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time.  - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the customer to different teams across Halte

As a South American Launch Specialist, you'll be one of the first people on the ground establishing Halter's presence across the region — and you'll own what it means to bring Halter to producers in Argentina, Uruguay, and Brazil for the first time.

You'll lead the rollout of Halter on new operations end-to-end: training cattle and operators, solving problems in the field, and supporting producers as they get started. You'll work directly with ganaderos and pecuaristas — on the estancia, on the fazenda, in the campo — building the onboarding experience that every future customer in the region will inherit.

This role is partially field-based. Expect roughly a 70/30 split toward time on the ground, with regular travel across Argentina, Uruguay, and Brazil. You'll be with customers where they run their cattle, and the quality of what you build depends on you being there and understanding their operations deeply..

It's practical, hands-on, and highly ownership-driven. Every operation is different, and you'll tailor each deployment to help producers build confidence with Halter. You'll work closely with our Product team to make sure Halter meets the realities of South American ranching, not a playbook borrowed from somewhere else.

 - Travel to estancias and fazendas across Argentina, Uruguay, and Brazil to deploy Halter in person

 - Work directly with producers to bring Halter into their operation and support day-to-day use

 - Lead training that fits the operation: practical, straightforward, and useful

 - Act as the main point of contact during deployment, giving customers a clear, reliable owner

 - Partner closely with Sales, Support, Product, and Operations to keep deployments coordinated across borders

 - Keep deployments on track by managing timelines, aligning resources, and clearing blockers

 - Solve problems quickly and adapt plans as conditions change — language, terrain, and infrastructure will all vary

 - Spot patterns in the field and feed them directly to Product to shape how Halter works for the region

 - Set customers up with the confidence and foundation needed for long-term success with Halter

 - Whatever else it takes: This is an early-stage market entry. You’ll do what needs doing to make Halter succeed in South America.



WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience working with customers: whether onboarding, supporting, deploying, or managing complex rollouts

 - Genuine comfort with travel and field work

 - Fluency in Spanish and English, Portuguese is a bonus.

 - Confidence operating independently and keeping priorities organized

 - The ability to coordinate moving pieces and keep things progressing without constant oversight

 - A practical, solutions-focused mindset when challenges come up

 - Comfort working cross-functionally: pulling in the right people and keeping everyone aligned

 - Clear, straightforward communication

 - Good judgment and the ability to adapt when plans change

 - A genuine care for the people we serve and the quality of the work

 - Agriculture or cattle ranching experience, especially with extensive grazing systems

English proficiency is a requirement for this role. The recruitment process will include interviews conducted in English, and a significant part of the day-to-day work will also be conducted in English.  - Startup or high-growth environment experience

 - Experience working in ag-tech

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the Southern region of Arkansas. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the customer to different teams across Halt

THE OPPORTUNITY 

At Halter, we're on a mission to enable farmers and ranchers to run the most productive and sustainable operations on earth. Argentina is one of our most important next frontiers. We're entering the market with high ambition and a small team that needs to move fast, learn quickly, and build trust from the ground up. We're hiring a People & Performance Partner to build the people foundation from zero to one.




THE ROLE

You'll partner with local leaders and the global P&P team to stand up the core people infrastructure for a new market — then keep raising the bar as the team scales.

In practice, that means:

 - Establishing people processes, leadership rhythms, documentation, and workflows for a high-performing new market team

 - Coaching managers through feedback, performance conversations, development, and early employee relations matters

 - Owning onboarding quality so new starters understand the mission, operating model, and cultural bar from day one

 - Running people logistics — systems, documentation, compliance, and employee information

 - Supporting market-entry operations: office setup, field-team logistics, local vendor coordination, fleet and vehicle processes

 - Staying close to the ground and feeding signal back to People, Talent, Commercial, and leadership

Responsibilities will evolve. This is an early-stage role — you'll be part of making the whole thing work.

About Halter

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association
meetups.

 

This role covers the Central region of Montana. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.

 


WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattlemans, Stockmans associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the customer to different teams across Halter.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the Northern region of Arizona. Frequent travel is expected as apart of this role.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the customer to different teams across Halte

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a driven, high-performing Account Manager to join the momentum and help shape the future of farming in the West Coast region. This is an opportunity to positively disrupt an industry and pioneer groundbreaking change, working with some of the highest-performing dairy farms in New Zealand. Serving as the primary point-of-contact for Halter customers, you will be passionate about driving farmer success for one of the world’s fastest-growing companies that will transform how they farm to become leaders in productivity and sustainability. You will be backed by a team of exceptional people on the ground in the South Island and at Halter’s Auckland HQ, to ensure this is the best job you’ll ever have.


Location - This role is to be based anywhere in the West Coast region. Frequent travel is required as part of the position.

 


WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Revenue Retention & Expansion: You will own the retention, renewals and expansion targets of Halter’s existing revenue in the region.

 - Ensure farmers are extracting full value from Halter to achieve their goals and ultimately understand the impact it’s having on their farming business.

 - Account Management: Responsible for renewing customer agreements and expanding the revenue of existing Halter customers, by adding value in every interaction to drive on-farm goals and performance.

 - Deployment: Supporting the onboarding, training and implementation of the Halter system on customers' farms, ensuring all relevant farm owners, managers, and workers are able to successfully use the system.

 - Relationship Building: Proactively cultivate genuine and trustworthy relationships with farmers, their teams, and families, fostering strong connections and understanding.

 - Farmer Success: Strategically partnering with customers to establish clear business goals, timelines, priorities and metrics of success.

 - Problem-Solving: Provide prompt and effective communication and support to farmers and team members, addressing technical or operational challenges with expertise and efficiency.

 - Community & Networking: Represent the Halter brand with pride, lead local discussion groups, and proactively build strong networks within the community for increased brand visibility and connections.

 - Customer Advocate: Acting as the voice of the customer and bridging the gap with our product teams to provide important context about what is happening on the ground with our farmers and their animals.

 - Technical Expertise: Working closely with our product teams to provide technical and practical advice from a farmer’s perspective on everything reproduction, pasture and agronomy.

 - Contribute to a positive team environment, supporting others to succeed and role modelling Halter’s Operating Principles.

 


WE’RE BACKING POTENTIAL OVER POLISH. THESE ARE THE TRAITS THAT MATTER MOST

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.

About Halter

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association
meetups.



This role covers the South East region of Wyoming. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattlemans, Stockmans associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the customer to different teams across Halter.

 - Laying the groundwork for the local sales function — helping to set and manage quotas, commissions and other sales management tasks as the team grows.

 - Coaching, mentoring and developing future sales staff to help drive their professional growth and reach targets as we scale the region.

 - Collaborating with Customer Success to ensure successful post-sales handoff, implementations, customer satisfaction and account renewal.

 - Providing support, insight and communication to help build and foster trusting and enduring relationships with customers as they wait for deployment.

 - Leveraging opportunities and participating in relevant industry/Halter events and demonstrations.

 - Building and leveraging industry relationships to establish and maintain Halter's brand in a brand-new market.

 - Focusing on the customer and their needs, providing feedback to help drive the product roadmap.

 - A complete end-to-end sales skill set with at least five years of experience.

 - Sales experience in the technology-based industry is preferred.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're building something special at Halter, and we need the right people on the road to make it happen. As a Junior Field Technician, you'll be a core part of our Field Team, keeping our collar fleet moving across farms throughout your dedicated region. You’ll serve as a key connection between what happens on-farm and the engineering team back in Auckland, making sure collars get to the right farms, are tracked accurately, and come back to HQ when needed.  You'll cover the length and breadth of the country, operating on a continuous farm visit loop. Expect to be on the move and spending up to 2–3 nights away from home per week.  

This is a fixed-term role where attitude is everything and we are on the hunt for an upbeat go-getter.

 - Build your daily travel plan and use route optimisation tools to hit every farm efficiently

 - Hit the road, driving between farms

 - Manage collar stock on customer farms, making sure levels are accurate and nothing slips through the cracks

 - Pack and dispatch urgent spare collars to farms that need them fast

 - Ship collars back to AKL HQ and keep logistics running smoothly

 - Conduct hardware audits and trials on customer farms.

 - Be a positive, professional face of Halter when you're on-farm with our customers
